why: The PATHS in this file are re-derived every run and are here only so a drift has something to disagree with. The READING is not re-derivable: what a file DOES with the stamp it matched is a human reading, so it is a datum and never a guess. An unread file is `reads: null` and the gate SHORTFALLs on its own debt rather than passing over it.

`anchored` applies to a `time` reading alone. True means the instant comes from a stamp owner that bounds the digit run and range-validates the components (`DexClock.fileStamp`, a local `_mkTMs` / `stampMk`, `writers.file_start_stamp`, `nightqc.floating_stamp_s`). False means the file slices the digits into a bare `Date.UTC` or `strptime` itself. Every other reading computes no instant, so §∅ makes its `anchored` null.

The parent census's predicate was the literal source text `\d{14}`, so it saw one spelling of one read. Twelve files here spell the same fourteen digits out and were invisible to it — among them two the parent credited as FIXED, because a file with two readers leaves a spelling-keyed census when one reader is repaired.

adapters/resmed-edf.js.note: `FNAME_RE` stays the accept test for the ResMed per-stream grammar; `stampOf` takes the instant from the owner beside it. The pattern decides membership, never a time.

capture-host/loss_audit.py.note: The only sum-to-14 spelling is prose: the comment recording that the stamp is read anchored through `writers.file_start_stamp`, and that the `_(\d{14})_` search which stood there was the audit F5 defect.

capture-host/nights_index.py.note: Delegates to `nightqc.floating_stamp_s`, which owns the bound and the range check for the capture host.

capture-host/parse_dat.py.note: `oxy_start_dt` searches an UNBOUNDED `(\d{14})` over the basename and feeds `strptime`, which range-validates and raises. The run is still not bounded and the scan runs left to right, which is the defect `clock.js` §BOUND names: a 14-digit device id wins over the session stamp beside it. This is NOT the §∅ verdict board #1181 reached on the same function — a Format-A `.dat` header carries no absolute time, so the name is the only witness and the function returns None rather than inventing one. Clean on fabrication, unanchored on bounding.

capture-host/ppg_grid_check.py.note: `_O2_PPG_RE` admits an O2Ring PPG filename. No instant is computed from the digits.

capture-host/writers.py.note: Prose in `file_stamp` naming the two unanchored `_(\d{14})_` searches it replaced. The writer itself is the stamp's source, not a reader of it.

clock.js.note: THE OWNER. `fileStamp` scans from the right, bounds the digit run to a whole token and range-validates the components before `Date.UTC`.

cpapdex-app.js.note: Routes the ResMed filename stamp through `CpapEdf.stampMk`, the node-local owner.

cpapdex-edf.js.note: `_mkTMs` is the CPAP node's own range-checked maker. This bundle does not carry `clock.js`, so a node-local owner is the deliberate variant, not a mirror to remove.

dex-ingest.js.note: Two readers in one file: the stamp is part of the device-key accept pattern at the first site, and `stampMs` converts it through `_stampMk`, which refuses an out-of-range year and a rolled calendar day.

oxydex-dsp.js.note: `_o2BinStartMs` delegates to `fileStamp`; the sum-to-14 spelling that remains is the comment recording why — a bare run took the first fourteen digits of a longer one, and the scan now runs from the right.

pat-classic-vs-fused.js.note: `stampOf` keeps the pattern as the accept test, because it encodes that the stamp sits before the stream suffix, and takes the instant from `DexClock.fileStamp`. The value is the key `nearest()` picks a session by, so a fabricated instant would pick the wrong session.

pat-feasibility.js.note: Role patterns key a session by the stamp string; `stampMs` length-tests it as the §∅ leg and converts through `_mkTMs`.

resp-acc-analysis.js.note: `sessionStamp` returns `{ day, hhmmss }` as STRINGS and is exported for gating which nights a paper may see. No instant.

sensor-trio-night.js.note: Role patterns carry the stamp as a key; `stampMs` length-tests and converts through `_mkTMs`.

sensor-trio-power-analysis.js.note: Same shape as its two siblings: a role key, then `stampMs` through `_mkTMs`.

sigma-no-reference-analysis.js.note: Same shape again, and its own comment states the stronger rule: the night a file belongs to comes from its first data row, not its name.

tools/acc-acc-control.mjs.note: Normalises both spellings, then slices the 14 digits into a bare `Date.UTC` with no range check, and the result buckets a night noon-to-noon for a control figure.

tools/cpap-corpus.mjs.note: `stampOf` slices the matched date and time into a bare `Date.UTC`. The seconds it returns order the session clusters, so a rolled component mis-clusters a mask-off/on pair.

tools/stamp-consumer-census.mjs.note: THE INSTRUMENT SITS IN ITS OWN POPULATION, and it belongs there. Its predicate admits a file by the spelling and computes no instant, which is exactly an accept test. Its own sum-to-14 runs are the header prose, the selftest fixtures and the atom pattern itself. Excluding it would be the one hole a census cannot afford: the file that decides membership would be the only one nobody re-derives. It entered the population the moment git tracked it, which is also the measurement that found this.

tools/cpap-sa2-agreement.mjs.note: `SA2_STAMP`'s groups become a `YYYY-MM-DD` night key. No instant.

tools/device-stability.mjs.note: `parseName` returns the stamp as a string beside vendor, model, device id and stream. The instants this tool compares come from the stream's own rows, not from the name.

tools/oracle-ecg-firmware-rr.mjs.note: The stamp is the session key the oracle pairs an ECG with its firmware RR by.

tools/pat-window-oracle.mjs.note: `tok` is a join key, and an ECG with no token is REPORTED rather than dropped — an unparseable name is an absence of a key, not of a recording.

tools/ppg-foot-residual-sweep.mjs.note: Only the date half is used, as a `YYYY-MM-DD` per-night bucket key. No instant.

tools/pulse-agreement.mjs.note: The stamp names the session a PPG file belongs to.

tools/trio-batch.mjs.note: Six full-name patterns bound the run, so the left-scan defect is absent, but `parse14` and `parse8_6` slice into `utc`, which is `Date.UTC` with no component validation. `nightKeyOf` then buckets the corpus plan off that value.

tools/wearable-sync.mjs.note: Matches both spellings explicitly, per the Clock Contract's vendor-by-regex rule, then slices the groups into a bare `Date.UTC`. `nightOf` buckets evening-owns-the-night off the result.
